claims: Transfuse packed red blood cells for symptomatic anemia (hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL, hematocrit 24.2%).
Monitor hemoglobin/hematocrit and vital signs for ongoing bleeding and transfusion response.
Assess and manage acute kidney injury with creatinine 5.1 mg/dL and BUN 57 mg/dL, including strict intake/output and volume status.
Assess for hyperkalemia and renal acidosis (bicarbonate 17 mEq/L, anion gap 15 mEq/L, potassium 4.3 mEq/L) and repeat basic metabolic panel.
Repeat basic metabolic panel and renal function tests within 24 hours.
Continue phenytoin with monitoring of free/total phenytoin level (currently 1.5 ug/mL) and seizure precautions.
Continue venous thromboembolism prophylaxis with sequential compression devices or pharmacologic prophylaxis as appropriate.
Maintain fall precautions and bed rest with assistance for mobility given high fall risk and bedfast status.
Perform skin assessment and pressure ulcer prevention for existing impaired skin (1.5 cm x 1 cm) and Braden score indicating risk.
Continue hemodynamic monitoring with arterial line and maintain mean arterial pressure goals, avoiding hypotension (recent MAP 67-75 mmHg).
